clue.text: I can move over specially to keep wife warmer

indicators.note: to keep says the reworked letters hold the next piece inside them
specially here means arranged in a special way, so the letters of these words are reworked

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone politely asks a partner to shift along so they can keep their wife cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially' rearranges ICANMOVEOVER, and 'to keep' puts W (wife) inside the result to make MICROWAVE OVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A microwave oven is a kitchen appliance used to heat food, so it is a warmer.

clue.text: Sum up business quickly for a Parisian citizen

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
vite is French for quickly

explanation.surface: A French accountant is asked to tot up a firm's figures in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SUM into MUS; add CO (company) and VITE, French for 'quickly', which is what 'for a Parisian' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muscovite is an inhabitant of Moscow, so a citizen of the Russian capital.

clue.text: Muscles contributing to physical fitness

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Muscles help a person keep fit, a plain gym-poster statement.
explanation.definitionFit: The calf is the fleshy back of the lower leg, made of muscles; the plural definition stands for the muscle group.

clue.text: Better you're regularly in the fresh air

parts.note: to better someone is to outdo them

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second and fourth

parts.note: its alternate letters give the second piece

explanation.surface: A claim that you are generally improved by being outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb here, OUTDO, not a comparative; 'regularly' takes O and R from YOU'RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor describes something happening outside, under the open sky rather than in a building.

clue.text: Military medal worn under Australian's coat, etc.

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means this part comes below the other one
the coat of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: its outer letters give the first piece
DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military decoration
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: A soldier pins a decoration beneath an Australian's jacket, and so forth.
explanation.walkthrough: The DSO (Distinguished Service Order) is a British decoration; in a down clue 'under' puts it and 'worn' below the coat of the Australian.
explanation.definitionFit: And so on is the spoken equivalent of the abbreviation for et cetera, meaning more of the same.

clue.text: Electronic expertise behind Spielberg film's audio equipment

parts.note: art is skill or expertise
your behind is your rump
E.T. is Steven Spielberg's 1982 film about an alien

explanation.surface: Technical wizardry went into the sound kit for a Spielberg movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a position word but is the noun RUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear trumpet is an old hearing aid, a horn held to the ear to collect sound.

clue.text: Crook's not in residence

indicators.note: not here means without, so the following letters are dropped

parts.note: a crook is a villain
the letters taken out

explanation.surface: The criminal is out, not at home.
explanation.walkthrough: VILLAIN loses IN; the 's of 'Crook's' is the link 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country house, a kind of residence.

clue.text: Drink and lace ornament on a dresser

parts.note: to neck a drink is to gulp it down
to lace shoes is to tie them

explanation.surface: A bottle of something and a frilly doily sit on a piece of bedroom furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dresser' looks like the furniture but means a person who dresses smartly.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is decorative neckwear worn by someone getting dressed up.

clue.text: Policeman turned up caveman's fingers

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Stig of the Dump is the caveman of Clive King's children's novel

explanation.surface: A detective finds the fingerprints of a prehistoric man.
explanation.walkthrough: Stig is the caveman boy in the British children's book 'Stig of the Dump'; 'turned up' reverses STIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits are fingers (and toes), from the Latin for finger.

clue.text: Wrapped in cotton wool, American was rude to nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the first piece holds the second inside

parts.note: to be rude to someone is to insult them

explanation.surface: A rude American is rude to nurses while cosseting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wrapped in cotton wool is to be shielded from harm, insulated from the world.

clue.text: Old hand perhaps about fifty and in charge

parts.note: re means about, concerning
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A veteran of about fifty takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hand' suggests a veteran; it is literally an ancient hand, such as a saint's preserved in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a surviving fragment of the past, such as part of a saint's body kept for veneration.

clue.text: Star backs out of Jumanji, afraid to travel

indicators.note: the backs of words are their last letters, taken from each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A film star pulls out of the Jumanji movie because they fear flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs out of' reads as withdraws, but takes the back letters of the next four words.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a celebrity worshipped by fans, a star.

clue.text: Just as rich after being taken to the cleaners?

definitions.text: Just as rich after being taken to the cleaners?

parts.words: Just as rich after being taken to the cleaners?
parts.note: taken to the cleaners usually means fleeced of money; here it is literal laundering, after which the dyes stay just as rich

explanation.walkthrough: Being taken to the cleaners is an idiom for losing all your money, so 'rich' seems financial; it is about colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Colourfast fabric keeps its dye when washed, so its hues stay as vivid as before.

clue.text: Travelling abroad, Sam's a man on a mission

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: part of the fodder
part of the fodder, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Sam is heading overseas as an envoy on official business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling abroad' reads as the envoy's journey, but 'abroad' is fodder; the 'a' before the definition is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador heads a diplomatic mission, the embassy, in a foreign country.

clue.text: Nearly naked sportsman with boil gently squeezes

indicators.note: squeezes means holds tightly, so the first piece grips the second inside it

parts.note: to simmer is to boil gently

explanation.surface: A near-naked athlete gets an abscess that someone squeezes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boil' looks like a skin complaint but is the cooking verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitive swimmer races wearing only a small costume, so is nearly unclothed.

clue.text: Candidate number one's last to vote

parts.note: spoken by the one in question, one's own is mine

indicators.note: last to means the final letter of the next word

parts.note: its last letter is taken

explanation.surface: The leading contender is the final person to cast a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' looks like the frontrunner; NO and 'one's' (MINE) are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward for election or an award, a candidate.

clue.text: More tear cheap paper

parts.note: new can mean another, additional, as in a new round
to tear is to rush, to sprint

explanation.surface: Further rips appear in a flimsy sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' looks like a rip but is the verb for dashing, SPRINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is the low-grade, inexpensive paper that newspapers are printed on.

clue.text: Horse in box comes back fine

indicators.note: comes back means the whole assembly is read in reverse
in says the horse is placed inside the box before everything is turned round

parts.note: the box and the tele are both slang for television
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A horse returns to its stall in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts NAG into TELE, making TNAGELE, and 'comes back' reverses all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined, fine in the sense of stylish.

clue.text: University dons resend after mix-up; I get it, finally

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the jumbled letters wrap around the next piece
after a mix-up the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: University lecturers resend a document after confusion, and someone finally understands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like lecturers but is the verb: the anagram ENDSER wears U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An end user is the person who finally receives and uses a product, at the end of the supply chain.

clue.text: Buying and selling clubs provided Trump with turnover

indicators.note: a turnover flips something over, so all the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
if means provided that
to trump is a dated British slang word for breaking wind

explanation.surface: A trade deal involving clubs, provided Trump gets a cut of the revenue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' looks like the US president; in British slang a trump is a fart.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic means illicit trade, the dealing in goods, as in drug trafficking.

clue.text: Fewer manoeuvres when a yankee's on it?

definitions.text: Fewer manoeuvres when a yankee's on it?

indicators.note: manoeuvres means moves around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American motorway is so straight that drivers need to steer less.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes an American road; 'yankee' also gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeway is a US highway, long and straight enough that a driver makes fewer turns.

clue.text: What might alcoholic's yen be? To give up

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: a drinker's craving might be for the Japanese rice wine
second meaning: to abandon or renounce

explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like Japanese money but means a longing; split the answer into two words and it names what a drinker longs for.
explanation.definitionFit: To forsake is to abandon or renounce something, to give it up.

clue.text: Communist over in New York after revolution over there

indicators.note: a revolution is a turning, so all the pieces are reversed

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist

indicators.note: in places the cricket over within the New York abbreviation

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A communist goes across to New York after an uprising in a distant land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside NY; 'revolution' looks political but reverses REDNOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old word for something at a distance, over there.

clue.text: Servants duke has start to talk with affected manners

parts.note: to have is to own

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: its first letter is used
airs are pretentious manners, as in putting on airs

explanation.surface: A duke's servants begin talking with pretension.
explanation.walkthrough: In grand British houses the servants lived and worked below stairs, so 'downstairs' names them as a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Downstairs is a collective term for household staff, in contrast with the upstairs family.

clue.text: Bear up after women cry

indicators.note: after says this part follows the first one
in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the famous bear of A A Milne's stories

explanation.surface: A bear stands up after some women scream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is not an endure verb but the bear Pooh, reversed by 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud shout of joy or excitement.

clue.text: Second joke delivered positively

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: A second gag goes down well with the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun means presented with a favourable slant, as a press officer puts a positive spin on news.

clue.text: Cheeky blighter?

parts.note: a blighter is a rascal, but read literally it is something that blights the cheeks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky blighter' sounds like a scamp, but the clue means a spoiler of cheeks, the skin condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin complaint of spots that disfigures the face, especially the cheeks.

clue.text: Nag that's unhappy with saddle over its middle

indicators.note: over its middle says the next piece is laid over and replaces the central letter

parts.note: unhappy means sad
a col, or saddle, is a dip in a mountain ridge

explanation.surface: An unhappy horse has a saddle put on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' and 'saddle' suggest a horse; a saddle is also a mountain pass, COL, replacing the A of SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold is to tell off or keep finding fault, to nag.

clue.text: Farm is iron-clad business, according to a model

indicators.note: clad means covered, so the iron goes around the outside

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a ranch is a large farm

explanation.surface: A farm is a rock-solid business, by some template.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron-clad' reads as guaranteed, but splits into the chemical symbol for iron and 'clad', which wraps that symbol around the farm and 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a business run under licence to a set template, like a fast-food chain outlet.

clue.text: Censure for macho types in court, making it up

parts.note: a rap is a rebuke, censure
pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: in means the macho types go inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: he-men are macho types

explanation.surface: Tough guys get told off in court and then make up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making it up' sounds like inventing, but means reconciling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapprochement is the re-establishing of friendly relations, especially between nations, so reconciling.
